沙鈴以握柄持拿，透過搖動使內部顆粒撞擊容器發聲。初學可先單手握柄，前後搖動；多數: A maraca is held by its handle and shaken so that the grains inside strike the container. Beginners can start with one hand on a handle, shaking back and forth; in most settings the instrument is used in pairs, one in each hand shaken together, though some styles use only one. With the natural gourd type you can use a natural grip; with a wooden handle, hold the end of the handle.
沙鈴以搖動使內部顆粒撞擊容器內壁發聲，主要承擔節奏，突出拍點。量測顯示其頻率響應: The maraca sounds when it is shaken and the grains inside strike the wall of the container; it mainly carries the rhythm and marks the beat. Measurements show its frequency response lies between 3000 Hz and 10000 Hz. Volume and timbre depend on the filler and the material of the container, and it is played by shaking; it is usually used in pairs, though some styles use a single one. Unlike idiophones that sound when struck, the maraca sounds by shaking.
沙鈴常見於加勒比海與拉丁音樂，也偶見於搖滾音樂。拉丁流行音樂中，它多用於古巴頌樂: The maraca is common in Caribbean and Latin music and occasionally appears in rock. In Latin pop it is used mostly in Cuban son, guaracha, danzón, salsa, bomba, mambo, samba, cumbia and calypso; bomba can use a single maraca, the others mostly a pair shaken together. It also appears in indigenous and Afro-Brazilian spiritual settings, such as the toré ritual of the Tabajara in Brazil, the healing rituals of pajelança in the north, and the ceremonies of Andean healers, alongside chants, dance and healing.
沙鈴琴身可為皮革、木頭、塑膠或合成材料製成，現代球體常以木製握柄穿過殼體孔洞組成: The body of the maraca may be leather, wood, plastic or synthetic; the modern ball is often a wooden handle pushed through a hole in the shell. Others use a calabash or gourd as the body, the first shaken with a natural grip and the second fitted with a handle. The sounding material is usually small stones inside, and the material and filler affect timbre and volume. Some traditional maracas have human hair fixed at the top, a cut opening, and scarlet ibis feathers inserted; Puerto Rico uses the fruit of the higüera, and other regions use tin, wood, leather or synthetic materials.
沙鈴起源於前哥倫布時期，見於南美洲與加勒比海原住民的儀式與溝通。民族誌記載其發明: The maraca dates from before Columbus and appears in the ritual and communication of the indigenous peoples of South America and the Caribbean. Ethnography links its invention to the Arawak and the Taíno. In the eighteenth century the Jesuit missionary José Gumilla recorded maracas among Arawak-speaking peoples of the Orinoco basin. They also appear among the Tupinambá in divination and among the Guaraní. Early instruments were made from gourds or calabash; modern ones have a leather, wooden or plastic ball with a wooden handle inserted and small stones inside. The design varies by region: Puerto Rico uses the higüera fruit, other regions tin, wood, leather or synthetic materials, and the contents and materials affect timbre and volume. Andean healers use them in healing rituals too.
沙鈴（Maracas）是體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 112: The maracas are an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 112.13, usually played in pairs and shaken by the handle so that the grains inside strike the container. They are common in Caribbean and Latin American music and occasionally in rock; in Native American and Afro-Brazilian spiritual traditions they are used in ritual, healing and calling on spirits.
